sections.heading: Why Foggy Windows Happen and Why You Should Act Quickly
sections.body: Foggy windows are caused by the failure of the airtight seal that holds the insulated glass unit together. When that seal breaks down, outside air and moisture penetrate the space between the glass panes, forming condensation that appears as a persistent fog or haze. Over time, mineral deposits from the trapped moisture etch the glass surface, making the damage permanent if left unaddressed. Beyond the visual nuisance, a failed seal dramatically reduces the thermal performance of your window, forcing your HVAC system to work harder and driving up energy bills. In Arlington, where temperatures swing from humid summers to cold winters, a compromised window seal creates real comfort and cost problems. Acting quickly by scheduling a professional assessment limits further deterioration and often allows the insulated glass unit to be replaced without touching the surrounding frame, saving significant time and money compared to a full window replacement.

faq.q: Can foggy windows be repaired without replacing the entire window frame?
faq.a: Yes. In most cases only the insulated glass unit itself needs to be replaced. The existing frame, sash, and hardware can remain in place, which significantly reduces the cost and time of the repair compared to a full window replacement.

faq.q: How long does a foggy window repair take in Arlington?

The on-site installation typically takes one to two hours per window. Commercial projects with multiple units may require additional scheduling, which we outline in advance.
